title: U.S. House · Wisconsin's 8th Congressional District
area: Northeastern Wisconsin, including Green Bay and Appleton.

context.text: Incumbent Tony Wied (R) advanced from the Republican primary unopposed. Rick Crosson defeated Mark Scheffler and Katrina deVille in the Democratic primary.

candidates.name: Tony Wied
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Republican primary unopposed.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for Wisconsin's 8th Congressional District (since November 2024)

summary.text: Tony Wied is the Republican incumbent for Wisconsin's 8th District. A Green Bay-area businessman who operated Dino Stop gas stations and Little Caesars restaurants until selling the businesses in 2022, he won the 2024 special and general elections with President Trump's endorsement and was sworn in on November 12, 2024. He serves on the Agriculture, Small Business, and Transportation and Infrastructure committees.

background.text: Born in Lincoln, Nebraska; raised in Green Bay, where his official biography says he has spent his entire life in Northeast Wisconsin.
Graduated from Notre Dame Academy in Green Bay in 1994 and played football at St. Norbert College in De Pere, earning a bachelor's degree in business and administration in 1998.
With his wife, Angela, operated several Dino Stop gas stations and convenience stores in Northeast Wisconsin and later opened several Little Caesars restaurants; the businesses were sold in 2022.

In his Ballotpedia survey he described himself as a political outsider with nearly three decades of experience starting and operating businesses, and said he was the only candidate endorsed by President Trump in the race.
Elected in 2024 to the seat vacated by Mike Gallagher; sworn in on November 12, 2024, and elected to a full term in the 119th Congress.
Assigned in 2025-2026 to the Committee on Agriculture, the Committee on Small Business and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure, according to Ballotpedia.
Lives in De Pere with his wife, Angela, and their four sons, according to his official biography.

priorities.text: In his 2024 candidate survey, said he would prioritize finishing the border wall, reinstituting the Remain in Mexico policy, and funding border agents.
Says he believes in reducing the size of government to let Americans live the American Dream.

positions.summary: 2024 candidate survey said he would prioritize finishing the border wall, reinstituting the Remain in Mexico policy, and ensuring border agents have funding to do their jobs.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture, the Committee on Small Business, and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (Aviation, Highways and Transit, and Water Resources and Environment subcommittees) in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.researchNotes: The cited priorities are from Wied's 2024 Candidate Connection survey; he has not completed a 2026 survey and no updated public statement of positions was found. Ballotpedia and Wied's House office list his House service as beginning in November 2024 (special election); his House committee page did not load, so committee assignments are from Ballotpedia.

candidates.name: Rick Crosson
candidates.ballotNote: Defeated Mark Scheffler and Katrina deVille in the Democratic primary.
candidates.currentRole: Retired U.S. Army Lieutenant Colonel; former Green Bay Area Public School District Board of Education member (left office 2025)

summary.text: Rick Crosson is the Democratic nominee for Wisconsin's 8th District. A retired U.S. Army lieutenant colonel and master Army aviator, he later spent nearly 20 years in logistics and transportation in Green Bay and served on the Green Bay Area Public School District Board of Education until 2025. He won the August 2026 Democratic primary with 35.2% and is running on affordability, accountability and results.

background.text: Born into a working-class family, according to his campaign website, which describes a lifetime of service; a news report says he comes from a line of military veterans.
Graduated from Lakes High School, earned a bachelor's degree from Seattle University in 1980 and a graduate degree from Golden Gate University in 1991.

Served in the U.S. Army from 1980 to 2000, retiring as a lieutenant colonel and master Army aviator; his campaign says he flew surveillance missions along the Iron Curtain and served as U.S. Military Liaison to Mexico, working from the embassy.
Held a diplomatic passport while serving as military liaison to the government of Mexico and served in command and staff positions in combat aviation units, per his Ballotpedia survey.

After retiring from the Army, spent nearly 20 years in logistics and transportation, first at Schneider National in Green Bay and later running a Wisconsin-based trucking company; Ballotpedia lists his profession as chief operating officer.
Served on the Green Bay Area Public School District Board of Education (at-large) until 2025; his campaign says he helped guide decisions on school funding, boundaries and a local referendum.

Has served on the Greater Green Bay YMCA Board, the Brown County Library Board and the UW-Stevens Point Business Advisory Council, per his campaign website; he is a father of three and grandfather of eight.
Announced his candidacy in September 2025 and won the August 11, 2026 Democratic primary with 35.2% over Mark Scheffler and Katrina deVille.

priorities.text: Says his three key campaign messages are healthcare as a fundamental human right, affordable housing and a livable wage in a stable economy, and a strong emphasis on education.
Says he is motivated to reestablish Congressional authority as a check and balance to what he calls executive overreach.
priorities.quote: I am motivated to unify this country by reestablishing Congressional authority as a genuine check and balance to executive overreach.

positions.summary: Candidate survey lists healthcare as a fundamental human right as one of his three key campaign messages.
Candidate survey lists a livable wage as part of his campaign focus on affordable housing and a stable economy.

record.text: Served on the Green Bay Area Public School District Board of Education (at-large) until leaving office in 2025.
